results.claim: Fixed-placement feasibility has an exact matching characterization, yielding an XP exact algorithm parameterized by the number k of bugs.
results.proof_sketch: Fix a multiset B of bugs and their host intervals. For each safe house v, let A(v) be the bugs hosted in N[v]. Construct a bipartite graph whose left side is the safe houses and whose right side consists of all nonempty subsets of B; join v to S exactly when S⊆A(v). A matching saturating all safe houses is precisely an assignment of distinct nonempty feasible signatures. Conversely, such signatures define each bug's monitored set. Thus one can test a placement by bipartite matching, or by the source's polynomial lexicographic test. Enumerating the binomial(n+k−1,k) multisets of k host locations gives an n^{k+O(1)} exact decision algorithm for OPT≤k.

results.claim: Regional information bound: for every X⊆V, at least ceil(log2(|X|+1)) bugs must be hosted in N[X]. Moreover, the optimum is additive over connected components.
results.proof_sketch: Every signature of a vertex in X uses only bugs whose hosts lie in N[X]=union_{x∈X}N[x]. If h bugs are hosted there, only 2^h−1 nonempty subsets of those bugs exist, so |X|≤2^h−1. If several sets X_i have pairwise disjoint N[X_i], their bounds add. For components, no bug can hear across components, so restricting any solution to each component gives a solution there. Conversely, componentwise solutions can be united: their bug sets are disjoint, and nonempty signatures from different components therefore cannot coincide. Hence OPT(G)=sum_C OPT(C).

results.claim: If every connected component C has a universal safe house, then OPT is exactly sum_C ceil(log2(|C|+1)), computable in polynomial time.
results.proof_sketch: The information bound applied to a component C gives OPT(C)≥ceil(log2(|C|+1)). If u is universal in C, put that many bugs at u. Every safe house can hear all of them, so assign the |C| houses arbitrary distinct nonempty subsets. This attains the lower bound. Component additivity proves the formula. Components and universal vertices can be found in polynomial time.

results.claim: Incidence-capacity lower bound: if rho=max_v |N[v]| and a solution has k bugs, then L(n,k)≤k rho, where L(n,k) is the minimum total cardinality of n distinct nonempty subsets of a k-element set.
results.proof_sketch: Let the signatures be S(v). Double-count incidences: sum_v |S(v)|=sum_b |M(b)|. A bug hosted at z monitors only a subset of N[z], so the right side is at most k rho. The left side is minimized by taking subsets in increasing cardinality. Explicitly, if s is least with sum_{j=1}^s binomial(k,j)≥n, then L(n,k)=sum_{j=1}^{s−1} j binomial(k,j)+s(n−sum_{j=1}^{s−1}binomial(k,j)). In particular, at most k signatures are singletons, so L(n,k)≥2n−k.

results.claim: The problem is exactly solvable on interval graphs of maximum degree at most two. For every connected component C of order n, OPT(C)=floor(n/2)+1; componentwise summation gives the general answer.
results.proof_sketch: A connected maximum-degree-two graph is a path or cycle. An interval graph has no induced cycle of length at least four: for a cycle interval with minimum right endpoint, both cycle neighbors contain that endpoint and hence intersect, creating a chord. Thus only paths and K3 occur, and OPT(K3)=2. For P_n, 2n−k≤sum_v|S(v)|≤3k, so k≥ceil(n/2). If n=2t and k=t, equality forces every bug to monitor a complete three-vertex neighborhood, all t singleton codes to occur, and every other code to be a pair. Cohosted bugs have identical monitored neighborhoods and therefore cannot have singleton codes. Bugs at adjacent hosts make both host vertices contain their two bugs; since those codes have size two, they coincide. Hence the t hosts would have to be distinct nonadjacent internal vertices, but P_{2t} has at most t−1 such positions. Thus k≥t+1. Bugs on all odd vertices attain the formula for odd paths; for even paths, add a bug at the last vertex and use singleton codes on hosts and adjacent pairs between them.

results.claim: Running the source greedy algorithm in both timeline directions and taking the better result is not exact, even on a connected symmetric instance: both runs use seven bugs while OPT=6.
results.proof_sketch: Take L1=[−2/5,0], L2=[−2/5,1], L3=[3/5,2], L4=[8/5,3], L5=[8/5,4], L6=[13/5,5], U=[7/2,23/2], and let Ri be the reflection of Li under x↦15−x. Exact execution adds bugs at processing/host positions (1,2),(2,3),(4,6),(6,7),(9,11),(11,13),(13,13), totaling seven; reflection gives the same trace in the opposite direction. Six bugs suffice: host a,b,c at L2,L3,L5 and d,e,f at R5,R3,R2. Give L1,…,L6 codes {a},{a,b},{a,b,c},{b},{b,c},{c}; give R1,…,R6 codes {f},{e,f},{d,e,f},{e},{d,e},{d}; and give U code {c,d}. These codes are legal, nonempty, and distinct. The four leftmost L-vertices have neighborhood exactly the six L-vertices and therefore require three bugs hosted there. The symmetric right region independently requires three bugs in its disjoint six-vertex neighborhood. Hence OPT≥6, proving OPT=6.

final_writeup:
The general approximation threshold remains unresolved. Neither the parent nor this revision supplies a polynomial-time approximation with ratio strictly below 2 for arbitrary interval families, or an appropriate matching inapproximability theorem. The fixed-k exact procedure is XP, not polynomial for unrestricted k; the exact formulas apply only to restricted classes; and the lower bounds do not establish approximation hardness. Therefore the audit's VALID_PARTIAL_PROGRESS target judgment and ACCURATE claimed-resolution judgment are accepted, and claimed_resolution remains PARTIAL.

All six audit-VERIFIED load-bearing claims are retained with their exact wording. Their proofs explicitly require nonempty, pairwise distinct signatures; component additivity is established in both directions using disjoint bug identities; the maximum-degree-two classification is made componentwise; and fixed-placement feasibility is global saturation matching, not a local capacity inference.

The symmetric 13-interval witness remains deliberately narrow. Exact simulation in each timeline direction uses seven bugs, while the displayed six-bug code system is feasible and two disjoint regional bounds force six. Thus it proves OPT=6 and that bidirectional greedy is not exact, with observed ratio 7/6. As the audit emphasizes, this does not refute any ratio strictly below 2 and does not meet the open target.

Three BugBank diagnostics were applicable and independently checked. The in-place Bellman-Ford witness prompted literal recomputation after each greedy placement rather than a frozen-state assumption. The equal-length scheduling witness confirms the logical distinction between nonoptimality and failure of an approximation guarantee. The triangle-with-leaf witness prompted retaining connectedness only at the component level. The remaining hits concern structures absent from these proofs and are dismissed individually.
